items.q: A 54-year-old woman presents with progressive difficulty standing from a seated position and combing her hair. Examination reveals violaceous, flat-topped papules over the dorsal metacarpophalangeal and proximal interphalangeal joints, along with purplish discolouration around her upper eyelids. Serum creatine kinase is 3,200 IU/L. What cutaneous sign is present over her knuckles?
items.exp: Gottron papules are violaceous, lichenoid flat-topped papules overlying the dorsal aspects of the MCP and PIP joints, pathognomonic of dermatomyositis. The purplish periorbital discolouration with oedema represents the heliotrope rash.
r: Correct: Gottron papules are violaceous papules over the knuckles characteristic of dermatomyositis.
Heliotrope rash affects the periorbital eyelids, not the knuckles.
Palmar erythema is seen in chronic liver disease, thyrotoxicosis and pregnancy.
Erythema marginatum is seen in acute rheumatic fever.
items.kp: Gottron papules are violaceous papules over the knuckles characteristic of dermatomyositis.
items.source: British Society for Rheumatology guidelines on adult idiopathic inflammatory myopathies

x.key: Gottron papules are violaceous papules over knuckles in dermatomyositis.

others.B: Heliotrope rash is on the eyelids.
others.C: Palmar erythema is in liver disease.
others.D: Erythema marginatum is in rheumatic fever.

x.pearl: Gottron sign refers to macular erythema over elbows and knees, whereas Gottron papules are raised lesions over knuckles.
x.clues: Proximal weakness, high CK, violaceous knuckle papules, periorbital rash.
x.ddx: Systemic lupus erythematosus, polymyositis, lichen planus, psoriasis.
x.mech: Complement-mediated microangiopathy and perivascular CD4+ lymphocytic infiltration of muscle and skin capillaries.
x.lo: Recognise the pathognomonic cutaneous signs of dermatomyositis.
x.rev: Gottron papules are violaceous knuckle lesions pathognomonic of dermatomyositis.

items.q: A 56-year-old woman is diagnosed with dermatomyositis based on typical cutaneous findings, proximal muscle weakness, and elevated muscle enzymes. What systemic investigation is mandatory as part of her initial specialist workup?
o: Age- and sex-appropriate malignancy screening (CT chest, abdomen and pelvis, mammography)
items.exp: Adult-onset dermatomyositis is strongly associated with underlying malignancy (paraneoplastic phenomenon in 20-30% of adult cases, including ovarian, breast, lung, colorectal and gastric cancers). Comprehensive age-appropriate cancer screening is mandatory at diagnosis.
r: Correct: Occult malignancy screening is mandatory in adult-onset dermatomyositis.
Cerebral angiography is unindicated without intracranial stroke symptoms.
Bone density scans assess osteoporosis, not paraneoplastic malignancy risk.
Gastric emptying studies assess gastroparesis, not initial myositis workup.
items.kp: Adult-onset dermatomyositis mandates comprehensive screening for occult malignancy.
items.source: British Society for Rheumatology guidelines on adult idiopathic inflammatory myopathies

x.key: Adult dermatomyositis mandates age-appropriate cancer screening.

others.C: DEXA does not screen for cancer.

x.pearl: Ovarian cancer has the highest relative risk association with dermatomyositis in adult women.
x.ddx: Paraneoplastic myopathy, primary polymyositis, drug-induced myopathy.
x.mech: Ectopic expression of muscle and epidermal antigens by tumour cells provokes cross-reactive autoimmune attack.
x.lo: State the mandatory screening requirement in adult-onset dermatomyositis.
x.rev: Adult dermatomyositis requires comprehensive screening for occult malignancy.

items.q: A 48-year-old man presents with progressive exertional dyspnoea, Raynaud phenomenon, non-erosive arthritis, mild proximal muscle weakness, and rough hyperkeratotic fissures on the radial aspects of his fingers ('mechanic's hands'). HRCT reveals fibrosing non-specific interstitial pneumonia. Which autoantibody is most likely positive?
items.exp: Antisynthetase syndrome is characterized by the constellation of myositis, interstitial lung disease, Raynaud phenomenon, inflammatory arthritis, and 'mechanic's hands'. Anti-Jo-1 (anti-histidyl-tRNA synthetase) is the most frequent and classic autoantibody marker.
r: Correct: Anti-Jo-1 is the hallmark antibody of antisynthetase syndrome.
Anti-centromere is associated with limited systemic sclerosis without interstitial lung disease.
Anti-mitochondrial antibody is specific for primary biliary cholangitis.
Anti-smooth muscle antibody is seen in autoimmune hepatitis.
items.kp: Anti-Jo-1 antibody characterizes antisynthetase syndrome with interstitial lung disease and mechanic's hands.
items.source: British Society for Rheumatology guidelines on adult idiopathic inflammatory myopathies

x.pearl: Interstitial lung disease in antisynthetase syndrome dictates overall prognosis and often requires cyclophosphamide or rituximab.
x.clues: Proximal weakness, mechanic's hands, ILD on HRCT, Raynaud phenomenon.
x.ddx: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, systemic sclerosis, mixed connective tissue disease.
x.mech: Autoantibodies directed against aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase enzymes trigger cytotoxic lung and muscle damage.
x.lo: Identify the autoantibody diagnostic of antisynthetase syndrome.
x.rev: Anti-Jo-1 antibody is associated with myositis, ILD, Raynaud and mechanic's hands.

next.text: Review antisynthetase syndrome and pulmonary myositis.

items.q: A 42-year-old woman presents with severe Raynaud phenomenon, skin thickening restricted to her fingers distal to the MCP joints (sclerodactyly), subcutaneous calcific nodules, esophageal dysphagia, and facial telangiectasia. Which autoantibody is most characteristic of this limited cutaneous systemic sclerosis phenotype?
items.exp: Limited cutaneous systemic sclerosis (CREST syndrome) features skin thickening restricted to the distal extremities and face, and is strongly associated with anti-centromere antibodies (>70%). Anti-Scl-70 and anti-RNA polymerase III are characteristic of diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis.
r: Correct: Anti-centromere antibodies characterize limited cutaneous systemic sclerosis (CREST).
Anti-Scl-70 (topoisomerase I) characterizes diffuse systemic sclerosis and severe lung fibrosis.
Anti-RNA polymerase III is associated with diffuse skin disease and scleroderma renal crisis.
Anti-Smith antibodies are specific for SLE.
items.kp: Anti-centromere antibodies are characteristic of limited cutaneous systemic sclerosis (CREST).
items.source: British Society for Rheumatology and British Health Professionals in Rheumatology guideline for the management of systemic sclerosis

x.key: Anti-centromere antibodies characterize limited systemic sclerosis.

others.C: Anti-RNA polymerase III links to renal crisis.

x.pearl: Patients with limited systemic sclerosis and anti-centromere antibodies carry late risk of isolated pulmonary arterial hypertension.
x.clues: Sclerodactyly, calcinosis, telangiectasia, distal skin involvement.
x.ddx: Diffuse systemic sclerosis, mixed connective tissue disease, morphea.
x.mech: Microvascular endothelial activation, perivascular lymphocytic infiltration, and uncontrolled fibroblast collagen synthesis.
x.lo: Differentiate serological profiles between limited and diffuse systemic sclerosis.
x.rev: Anti-centromere antibodies characterize limited cutaneous systemic sclerosis (CREST).

next.text: Review systemic sclerosis classification and serology.

items.q: A 50-year-old man with diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis presents with acute severe headache, visual blur and oliguria. Blood pressure is 220/120 mmHg. Serum creatinine has risen sharply from 90 to 380 micromol/L. Urinalysis shows 1+ protein and granular casts. Blood film shows microangiopathic haemolytic anaemia with schistocytes. What is the emergency treatment of choice?
o: Prompt initiation of an oral ACE inhibitor (such as captopril)
items.exp: Scleroderma renal crisis (SRC) is a medical emergency presenting with abrupt severe hypertension, acute kidney injury, and microangiopathic haemolytic anaemia. Immediate treatment with an ACE inhibitor (short-acting oral captopril titrated aggressively) reverses intrarenal vasoconstriction and preserves survival. Corticosteroids are contraindicated as high doses trigger SRC.
r: Correct: Oral ACE inhibitors (captopril) are the life-saving treatment of choice for scleroderma renal crisis.
Corticosteroids are strictly contraindicated as they precipitate and worsen scleroderma renal crisis.
Hydralazine does not block the intrarenal renin-angiotensin-aldosterone axis responsible for crisis.
Nephrectomy is unnecessary; renal recovery can occur with prompt ACE inhibition.
items.kp: Scleroderma renal crisis requires emergency treatment with oral ACE inhibitors; corticosteroids are contraindicated.
items.source: BSR and BHPR guideline for the management of systemic sclerosis

x.key: Emergency ACE inhibitor therapy is the cornerstone for scleroderma renal crisis.

others.C: Hydralazine fails to block intrarenal renin.

x.pearl: High-dose oral prednisolone (>15 mg daily) is an established trigger for scleroderma renal crisis in diffuse disease.
x.clues: Diffuse systemic sclerosis, acute malignant hypertension, AKI, schistocytes on blood film.
x.ddx: Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura, malignant essential hypertension, glomerulonephritis.
x.mech: Intrarenal vascular spasm and obliterative intimal proliferation activate massive renin release, inducing malignant hypertension.
x.lo: Recognise and manage scleroderma renal crisis with emergency ACE inhibitors.
x.rev: ACE inhibitors are the definitive life-saving therapy for scleroderma renal crisis.

items.q: A 45-year-old woman presents with persistent gritty sensation in both eyes, dry mouth requiring water to swallow dry crackers, and bilateral painless enlargement of her parotid glands. Schirmer test reveals 3 mm wetting in 5 minutes. Serum testing reveals positive anti-Ro (SSA) and anti-La (SSB) antibodies. Which long-term neoplastic complication requires monitoring?
o: B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma (mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue / MALT lymphoma)
items.exp: Primary Sjogren syndrome carries a 15- to 20-fold increased lifetime risk of developing B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma (most commonly marginal zone MALT lymphoma, often in the salivary glands). Persistent parotid swelling, purpura, low C4, and monoclonal paraprotein are red flags.
r: Correct: B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma (MALT) is the major long-term malignancy risk in Sjogren syndrome.
Osteosarcoma is not associated with Sjogren syndrome.
Medullary thyroid cancer is associated with MEN2, not Sjogren syndrome.
Renal cell carcinoma has no established link with Sjogren exocrinopathy.
items.kp: Sjogren syndrome carries a substantially increased risk of B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma.
items.source: British Society for Rheumatology guideline for the management of adults with primary Sjogren syndrome

x.key: B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma risk is elevated in primary Sjogren syndrome.

others.C: Medullary thyroid cancer relates to RET.

x.pearl: Persistent firm parotid gland enlargement or loss of previously elevated rheumatoid factor suggests lymphoma evolution.
x.clues: Dry eyes, dry mouth, parotid enlargement, anti-Ro/La positive.
x.ddx: MALT lymphoma, IgG4-related disease, sarcoidosis, amyloidosis.
x.mech: Chronic polyclonal B-cell hyperactivation in inflamed exocrine tissue progresses to monoclonal neoplastic expansion.
x.lo: Identify the neoplastic complication associated with primary Sjogren syndrome.
x.rev: Primary Sjogren syndrome is associated with increased risk of B-cell lymphoma.

next.text: Review Sjogren syndrome management and surveillance.

items.q: A 52-year-old woman with diffuse systemic sclerosis has worsening exertional breathlessness. Echocardiography shows normal left ventricular ejection fraction and normal pulmonary artery systolic pressure. High-resolution CT chest reveals bilateral basal reticulation, traction bronchiectasis, and ground-glass opacities. Which autoantibody is most predictive of this severe fibrosing lung disease?
items.exp: Anti-topoisomerase I (anti-Scl-70) antibodies are strongly associated with diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis and confer a high risk of rapidly progressive, severe fibrosing interstitial lung disease (NSIP or UIP pattern).
r: Correct: Anti-Scl-70 is strongly predictive of severe interstitial lung fibrosis in systemic sclerosis.
Anti-centromere is associated with limited disease and isolated pulmonary arterial hypertension, not pulmonary fibrosis.
Anti-mitochondrial antibody is specific for primary biliary cholangitis.
Anti-smooth muscle antibody is for autoimmune hepatitis.
items.kp: Anti-topoisomerase I (anti-Scl-70) correlates with progressive pulmonary fibrosis in systemic sclerosis.
items.source: BSR and BHPR guideline for the management of systemic sclerosis

x.key: Anti-Scl-70 predicts severe interstitial lung fibrosis in diffuse scleroderma.
x.pearl: Pulmonary fibrosis is now the single leading cause of mortality in patients with systemic sclerosis.
x.clues: Diffuse systemic sclerosis, basal traction bronchiectasis, ILD on HRCT.
x.ddx: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, antisynthetase syndrome, sarcoidosis.
x.mech: Aberrant TGF-beta activation and fibroblast transdifferentiation lead to excessive extracellular matrix collagen deposition in alveoli.
x.lo: Identify the autoantibody linked to interstitial lung disease in systemic sclerosis.
x.rev: Anti-Scl-70 antibodies predict fibrosing interstitial lung disease in systemic sclerosis.

items.q: A 36-year-old woman with severe Raynaud phenomenon develops progressive ulceration and gangrenous digital pitted scarring on her fingertips during winter months. Conservative measures and high-dose oral calcium channel blockers have failed. What intravenous vasodilator therapy is recommended for severe digital ischaemia?
items.exp: BSR and EULAR guidelines recommend intravenous iloprost (a prostacyclin analogue that promotes profound vasodilation and inhibits platelet aggregation) for severe, refractory digital ulceration and critical digital ischaemia in systemic sclerosis.
r: Correct: Intravenous iloprost is the evidence-based therapy for severe scleroderma digital ischaemia.
Heparin is an anticoagulant and does not provide active arteriolar vasodilation.
Epinephrine is a potent vasoconstrictor and would cause immediate digital infarction.
Tranexamic acid is an antifibrinolytic that promotes thrombosis and worsens ischaemia.
items.kp: Intravenous iloprost is indicated for severe digital ulceration and critical ischaemia in systemic sclerosis.
items.source: BSR and BHPR guideline for the management of systemic sclerosis

x.key: Intravenous iloprost treats critical digital ischaemia in systemic sclerosis.

others.B: Heparin is not a primary vasodilator.

x.pearl: Phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitors (e.g. sildenafil) and endothelin receptor antagonists (bosentan) are useful oral adjuncts for digital ulcers.
x.clues: Severe Raynaud, digital pitting scars, failed calcium channel blockers.
x.mech: Iloprost mimics prostacyclin, stimulating adenylate cyclase to produce smooth muscle relaxation and microvascular reperfusion.
x.lo: Select the intravenous vasodilator indicated for critical digital ischaemia in scleroderma.
x.rev: Intravenous iloprost is effective for severe digital ulcers in systemic sclerosis.

next.text: Review management of Raynaud and digital ulcers.

items.q: A 48-year-old woman presents with dry eyes and dry mouth. Examination of her eyes using rose bengal staining reveals extensive devitalised epithelial punctate lesions across the cornea and conjunctiva (keratoconjunctivitis sicca). What non-pharmacological and initial topical intervention is first-line?
o: Frequent preservative-free artificial tears and ocular lubricants
Immediate surgical punctal cautery without lubricant trials
items.exp: First-line management for keratoconjunctivitis sicca in Sjogren syndrome is regular, frequent application of preservative-free ocular lubricants (artificial tear drops during the day and lubricating ointments at night) to protect the corneal surface.
r: Correct: Preservative-free artificial tears and lubricants are first-line for dry eyes in Sjogren syndrome.
Atropine is an antimuscarinic that suppresses lacrimation and will worsen severe dry eyes.
Punctal occlusion is reserved for severe ocular dryness refractory to intensive topical lubrication.
Systemic corticosteroids are not indicated for uncomplicated keratoconjunctivitis sicca.
items.kp: First-line therapy for keratoconjunctivitis sicca in Sjogren syndrome is frequent preservative-free artificial tears.
items.source: BSR guideline for the management of adults with primary Sjogren syndrome

x.key: Preservative-free artificial tears are first-line for Sjogren dry eyes.
x.pearl: Preservatives (e.g. benzalkonium chloride) cause toxic epithelial damage when drops are instilled more than four times daily.
x.clues: Dry eyes, rose bengal staining, first-line management.
x.ddx: Blepharitis, Meibomian gland dysfunction, neurotrophic keratitis.
x.mech: Replenishing the aqueous and mucin tear film layers prevents desiccation and mechanical friction during blinking.
x.lo: Select the initial management of keratoconjunctivitis sicca in Sjogren syndrome.
x.rev: Preservative-free ocular lubricants are first-line for ocular dryness in Sjogren syndrome.

items.q: A muscle biopsy is performed in a 50-year-old man with proximal muscle weakness and elevated CK. Histopathology reveals endomysial mononuclear inflammatory infiltrates directly surrounding and invading non-necrotic muscle fibres, with overexpression of MHC Class I on sarcolemmal membranes. What is the diagnosis?
items.exp: Polymyositis is characterized histologically by endomysial inflammation with CD8+ cytotoxic T-lymphocytes directly invading non-necrotic myofibres that ubiquitously express MHC Class I. Dermatomyositis, by contrast, shows perivascular and perimysial CD4+ lymphocytic infiltrates with perifascicular atrophy.
r: Correct: Endomysial CD8+ inflammation invading non-necrotic fibres defines polymyositis.
Dermatomyositis features perimysial/perivascular inflammation and perifascicular atrophy.
Inclusion body myositis features rimmed vacuoles on Gomori trichrome stain and amyloid deposits.
Muscular dystrophy shows dystrophin absence, fibrofatty replacement and minimal inflammation.
items.kp: Endomysial CD8+ lymphocytic invasion of myofibres with MHC Class I expression defines polymyositis.
items.source: Oxford Textbook of Rheumatology: Inflammatory myopathies

x.key: Endomysial CD8+ infiltration of non-necrotic fibres characterizes polymyositis.
x.pearl: Perifascicular atrophy (hypotrophy of muscle fibres at the periphery of fascicles) is the histological hallmark of dermatomyositis.
x.clues: Proximal weakness, high CK, endomysial infiltrate invading non-necrotic fibres, MHC Class I upregulation.
x.ddx: Dermatomyositis, inclusion body myositis, immune-mediated necrotising myopathy.
x.mech: CD8+ cytotoxic T-cells recognise antigen presented by aberrant sarcolemmal MHC Class I, releasing perforin and granzyme.
x.lo: Differentiate the histological features of polymyositis from dermatomyositis.
x.rev: Polymyositis shows endomysial CD8+ invasion; dermatomyositis shows perimysial/perifascicular inflammation.
